references.text: The miraculous catch of fish after Jesus' resurrection, where the disciples cast the net on the right side of the boat at Jesus' command and make an enormous catch—a clear parallel to the miraculous catch in Luke 5.
The immediate context where Jesus tells Simon to cast the nets into deep water, and Simon obeys despite a night of unsuccessful fishing—this is the prelude to the great catch in verse 6.
The continuation of the account where the disciples call for help from the other boat because the catch was so large that the nets were beginning to break and the boats were starting to sink.

Ezekiel's prophetic vision of water flowing from the temple, where wherever the water flows there will be a great multitude of fish—an image of God's abundance and blessing, reflected in the miraculous catch of fish.

The psalmist praises the Lord for His many works and that the sea is full of creatures without number—God's sovereignty over creation and the riches of the sea, which Jesus demonstrates through the miraculous catch.

At the second miraculous catch of fish, Simon Peter dragged the net ashore filled with 153 large fish, and despite the quantity the net did not break—a contrast to Luke 5:6 where the nets were beginning to break.
Jesus' call of Simon, James, and John to become fishers of men—the great catch serves as a sign of their future mission.
